description: We are team "1 braincell, 2 people", participating virtually in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 at the Harohalli local event. Our challenge was to harmonize historical satellite data (MODIS and VIIRS) to create a seamless record of global wildfire activity. To solve this, we built a web application featuring a burning activity calendar and anomaly charts, designed to help emergency responders and scientists easily analyze historical fire patterns and better understand fire trends over time.
summary: MV-Sat harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS satellite data to create a continuous, sensor-agnostic record of wildfire activity from 2001 to 2025 for Canada and the US. By correcting the 6x detection bias between the two sensors, we provide a seamless timeline for emergency responders and scientists. The interactive web application features an interactive satellite hotspot map, a GitHub-style burning activity calendar, and anomaly charts comparing current data against multi-year averages. This tool empowers users to analyze historical fire patterns, track critical deviations, and make data-driven decisions for fire management.
details:
What it does: MV-Sat is a web application that visualizes harmonized historical wildfire data for Canada and the US (2001-2025). It features an interactive satellite map, a GitHub-style contribution calendar for fire intensity, and an analytics dashboard that charts historical anomalies against the 25-year average.
Intended Impact: This tool enables emergency managers, scientists, and land managers to understand long-term fire trends, identify unusually severe fire seasons, and use historical context to prepare for current and future wildfire threats.
Tools & Languages: Python, Streamlit, Pandas, Plotly, Folium, PyArrow, NumPy, Docker, GitHub.
Creativity: We successfully solved the sensor bias between MODIS (1km) and VIIRS (375m) by calculating an overlap ratio (6.00) and applying a bias correction to the historical data. The UI was designed with a custom glassmorphism aesthetic and an accessible color ramp.
